headline: India disowns Sheikh Hasina's remarks on Bangladesh's interim government
summary: The Indian government clarifies that a recent virtual press conference featuring the ousted Bangladeshi leader was a private initiative with no official state support.
details: India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified that the Indian government has no connection to the virtual press conference held by ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi.
During a regular press briefing on Friday, Jaiswal stated that the event was a completely private initiative and the Indian government played no role in its organization.
He emphasized that the government does not support any of the statements made on that platform, specifically those regarding the duly formed government of Bangladesh.
The clarification comes after Sheikh Hasina joined a press conference in New Delhi virtually to comment on the current administration in Bangladesh.
The move is seen as a diplomatic effort by India to distance itself from Hasina's criticisms of the interim government in Dhaka.
caption:
India has officially distanced itself from Sheikh Hasina's recent comments about Bangladesh's new government.

India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified that the Indian government has no connection to the virtual press conference held by ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in New Delhi.

During a regular press briefing on Friday, Jaiswal stated that the event was a completely private initiative and the Indian government played no role in its organization.

He emphasized that the government does not support any of the statements made on that platform, specifically those regarding the duly formed government of Bangladesh.

The clarification comes after Sheikh Hasina joined a press conference in New Delhi virtually to comment on the current administration in Bangladesh.

The move is seen as a diplomatic effort by India to distance itself from Hasina's criticisms of the interim government in Dhaka.

headline_marked: Shakib Al Hasan [[ready to return and face trial]] if given security
headline: Shakib Al Hasan ready to return and face trial if given security
summary: The former captain says he is willing to face murder and corruption charges in Bangladesh provided his safety is guaranteed.
details: Former MP and cricketer Shakib Al Hasan told Reuters he is ready to return to Bangladesh to face trial for murder and corruption charges if the government ensures his security.

Shakib, who has been living in the US with his family for nearly two years, described the murder case against him as 'ridiculous,' stating he was playing a match in Toronto on the day of the alleged incident.
He expressed a strong desire to return home immediately, or potentially in December alongside Sheikh Hasina, and hopes to play for Bangladesh in the 2027 ODI World Cup.
The cricketer revealed that he previously attempted to return to Bangladesh after receiving security assurances from the interim government, but was told to turn back mid-journey.
Shakib also mentioned that his bank accounts have been frozen for about a year and a half due to investigations, and he has been unable to visit his parents in Bangladesh for two years.
Despite suggestions that cutting ties with the Awami League and Sheikh Hasina might facilitate his return, Shakib stated he would not consider such a step.
caption:
Shakib Al Hasan is ready to face trial in Bangladesh—but only if his security is guaranteed.

Former MP and cricketer Shakib Al Hasan told Reuters he is ready to return to Bangladesh to face trial for murder and corruption charges if the government ensures his security.

Shakib, who has been living in the US with his family for nearly two years, described the murder case against him as 'ridiculous,' stating he was playing a match in Toronto on the day of the alleged incident.

He expressed a strong desire to return home immediately, or potentially in December alongside Sheikh Hasina, and hopes to play for Bangladesh in the 2027 ODI World Cup.

The cricketer revealed that he previously attempted to return to Bangladesh after receiving security assurances from the interim government, but was told to turn back mid-journey.

Shakib also mentioned that his bank accounts have been frozen for about a year and a half due to investigations, and he has been unable to visit his parents in Bangladesh for two years.

Despite suggestions that cutting ties with the Awami League and Sheikh Hasina might facilitate his return, Shakib stated he would not consider such a step.
